title: What is known about 1RB0LC_1RC0RA_1LA0LD_1LE0RB_1RB1LF_0LA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_1RC0RA_1LA0LD_1LE0RB_1RB1LF_0LA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves that between visits of state A the machine follows ten rewriting rules, for every tape, and halts exactly when state A reads a 1 with 1101 on its left. On the tape the rules move cursors through runs of 01, tripling the runs; cursors stall behind each other and collide, and whether a collision ever produces the halting pattern depends on the exact run lengths. No halt in 1011 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 71,228 cells have been visited and 35,574 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.483). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: Macro structure (observed)
claims.text: A layered bouncer: the tape is runs (01)^n separated by the marker 00110, in repeating pairs whose lengths triple from layer to layer ((9, 41), (27, 131), (81, 401), ...), while a block (10)^m at the left end grows and is spent.

claims.title: Ten rules between visits of state A
claims.text: From any configuration in state A the next one is given by R1 (A> 01 → 10 A>), R2 (A> 00 1<sup>k</sup> 0 → 1 0<sup>k</sup> A>1 1) or, when A reads 1, by the cells on its left (L1 … L8). Each is proved for every tape; L4 (1101 A>1) halts.

claims.title: Passes and rounds
claims.text: The right and left passes over a run of 01 and over a separator 00110 (the left pass moves two pairs across the separator), the left end, and nine rounds for all run lengths: a cursor moving through a run (a “1” b → a+2 “0” b → a+6 “1” b−2), crossing a separator, and two cursors vanishing.

claims.title: The case split is complete
claims.text: Running the machine from state A to the next visit of state A, branching on every unread cell, gives a finite tree: the ten rules and no other case; one halt.

claims.title: An exact run-length simulator
claims.text: Machine steps plus the two proved jumps over runs. Same step count at each of the 22,399 left-end events of the first 3·10<sup>8</sup> steps of the C simulator, same tape at the 409 compared. No halt in 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps (133,716 rounds); the C simulator: none in 10<sup>11</sup>.

claims.title: A cursor triples the runs it crosses
claims.text: A run of length b becomes 3b, 3b+4 or 3b+8 according to the parity of b and the mode in which the cursor entered (two modes); checked on 300 random run lists with the exact simulator.

claims.title: No halt in the first 6.03×10<sup>14</sup> steps of an accelerated run
claims.text: Observed, not proved: the accelerated simulator rsim.py ran 6.03×1014 steps from blank tape without reaching a halting transition. Its tape, state and head position were equal to those of a plain C simulator at 6 checkpoints, the last at 1.03×1010 steps. Of these steps, the part after the last checkpoint rests on the simulator alone, including 695 trip-level jumps: a jump applies many identical round trips at once after seeing the same tape shape recur with constant count changes, which is validated against direct simulation but not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt?
claims.text: Unknown. A halt needs the pattern 1101 A>1, which a single cursor among long runs never makes; it could only come from a collision of cursors with short runs, and which collisions happen depends on the exact run lengths and budgets.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The machine keeps a list of runs of 01 and sends cursors through it that triple every run they cross; the cursors live on a budget, stall and collide, and only a collision could stop the machine.

facts.text: describe the machine between visits of state A, for every tape; one of them halts.
without a halt (C simulator); the exact run-length simulator agrees with it at every left-end event of the first 3·10<sup>8</sup>.
No halt in the C simulator; 71,228 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
No halt in the accelerated simulator (observed, not proved; checked against direct simulation up to 1.03×10<sup>10</sup> steps).

sections.heading: Ten rules and one way to halt
html: Look at the machine only when it is in state A. If A reads 01 it flips the pair to 10 and moves on (R1). If it reads 00, the ones that follow are erased up to the next 0 and the head turns (R2). When A reads a 1 it is on its way left, and the few cells on its left decide: 10 is crossed (L1), 10101 becomes 01100 (L2), 111 becomes 101 (L3), three patterns turn the head right again (L5 to L8), and 1101 halts (L4). Lean proves each rule for every tape, and a finite case split shows there is no other case.

On the tape this looks as follows. Most of it is runs of 01, separated by the word 00110. The head flips the runs on its way right, crosses the separators, and turns at the first cursor, a single cell that breaks the pattern. On the way back each separator moves two pairs from its left to its right. After the round trip the cursor has moved: two rounds take it six cells to the right while eating two pairs of the run in front of it, so a run of length b is about 3b long once the cursor has gone through.

sections.heading: Cursors on a budget
html: Every round costs the first run one pair. A cursor in the first run feeds it, so a new cursor starts with a budget of about twice the run it first ate and then spends one pair per round. When the budget is gone, the first separator becomes a new cursor and the old one stops where it is. The tape so carries a stack of stalled cursors; each new one triples the runs up to the next stalled cursor and collides with it. Some collisions make both vanish, some leave one cursor or a new separator.

Exactly how a run grows depends on its parity and on the cursor’s mode: 3b, 3b+4 or 3b+8. That gives the layers seen in long runs: pairs of lengths (3, 11), (9, 41), (27, 131), (81, 401). The halting pattern 1101 next to the head cannot come from one cursor among long runs; it would take a collision with runs of length 0 or 1 in the wrong place. Whether the exact lengths ever line up that way is the open question. No halt in 1011 steps.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.483). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 71,228 cells (53,938 left of the start, 295 right), with a density of 1s of 0.499.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: Cursors walk through a list of runs of 01, tripling each run they cross, on a budget kept in the first run; seen in state A the machine is ten rewriting rules (Lean) with one halting pattern, 1101 A>1, which only a collision of cursors could produce (open).
